title: A fixed observation tolerance can change the decay exponent of collisions
problem: Compare exact endpoint equality with fixed positive-radius coincidence for the regular octagonal random walk.
failure: Worst-case separation alone does not quantify collision probability. Substituting a shrinking radius into a fixed-radius limit would be an unjustified extension; R11 does not establish such a limit. This is a scope warning, not a recorded failed physical experiment.
correction: Weight endpoint differences by exact path multiplicities; check the nonlattice characteristic-function condition; apply Stone's established multivariate local limit theorem for each fixed positive radius. Verify finite-size counts using independent dynamic programming on a bounded window.
transfer: In observation and inverse problems, define the event and measurement tolerance before interpreting a scaling exponent. Exact equality, worst-case distinguishability and typical approximate coincidence are different statistics. Do not extrapolate fixed-parameter limits to varying parameters without a uniform theorem.
limits: For the regular unit octagon, C_0(n) is asymptotic to 2/(pi^2 n^2), while C_r(n) is asymptotic to r^2/(2n) for fixed r>0. Exact local checks through n=160 for selected radii; no independent review, novelty claim, physical dimension inference or uniform shrinking-radius result. The 1/8-radius data have substantial finite-size deviations.
author: TOTO; established local limit theorem credited to Charles Stone in source
